## Summary

Addresses the two open PRs with the most unresolved review comments, applying all actionable fixes in a single follow-up PR.

**PR #83 — "test: elevate testing grade to 96/100" — 34 unresolved threads**
- `tests/e2e/chaos.spec.ts` (new): add top-level header comment; import `type Page` from `@playwright/test`; replace `any` with `Page` in `gotoHydrated`; replace the broad `expect(body).toBeVisible()` assertion with a meaningful `expect(getByTestId('home-text-error')).toBeVisible()`; replace `waitForTimeout(1000)` with a deterministic `expect(home-text-error).toBeVisible()` wait before retrying
- `vitest.integration.config.ts`: fix `__dirname` → ESM-safe `fileURLToPath(new URL(..., import.meta.url))` (was a `ReferenceError` in ESM project); wire `$env/dynamic/private` alias so integration tests can use the mock env; add required header comment
- `tests/integration/mocks/env.ts` (new): add top-level header comment; add all missing required keys (`XAI_TEXT_MODEL`, `XAI_IMAGE_MODEL`, `XAI_IMAGE_ENDPOINT_PATH`, `MAX_IMAGES_PER_REQUEST`, `DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE`, `GEMINI_*`) so `validateAppConfig` does not throw during integration runs
- `docs/evidence/2026-05-20/testing-evaluation-notes.md`: add Markdown purpose/why/info-flow header; fix "JSOM" typo → "JSDOM"; fix MD022 heading-spacing warnings
- `docs/evidence/2026-05-20/{proof-tape,seam-ledger,shaolin-lint}.json`: add `_purpose`/`_why`/`_infoFlow` metadata fields

**PR #85 — "feat: HTTP resilience — timeouts, exponential-backoff retry" — 17 unresolved threads**
- `src/lib/core/http-resilience.ts` (new): preserve caller `AbortSignal` in `fetchWithTimeout` so upstream cancellation and timeout both work; validate `maxAttempts >= 1` and `baseDelayMs >= 0` in `fetchWithRetry`; drain response body before sleeping on retry to avoid connection leaks; parse `Retry-After` as both delta-seconds and RFC-1123 HTTP-date
- `tests/unit/http-resilience.test.ts` (new): add `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` to `afterEach` to prevent stubbed `fetch` leaking across test files; remove no-op `expect(true).toBe(true)` placeholder; add tests for caller-signal propagation, HTTP-date `Retry-After`, and parameter validation

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings (svelte-check + TypeScript)
- [x] `npm test` — 401 tests pass, 1 skipped (unchanged integration gate)
- [x] New `http-resilience.test.ts` covers: caller signal propagation, HTTP-date Retry-After, parameter validation, vi.unstubAllGlobals cleanup

## Summary by Sourcery

Introduce shared HTTP resilience utilities and strengthen testing and evidence documentation to address prior review feedback.

New Features:
- Add shared HTTP resilience utilities for timeouts and exponential-backoff retries.
- Add chaos/fault-tolerance end-to-end tests covering API failure and recovery flows.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure integration tests can resolve $env/dynamic/private by aliasing to a mock env module with all required configuration keys.
- Handle Retry-After headers correctly for both delta-seconds and HTTP-date formats in HTTP retry logic.
- Preserve caller abort signals when applying HTTP timeouts so upstream cancellations are respected.

Enhancements:
- Document the testing architecture evaluation and grading outcomes in evidence notes, including the path to the target score.
- Add metadata JSON evidence files for proof tape, seam ledger, and linting artifacts.
- Improve HTTP retry behaviour by draining response bodies before retrying and validating retry parameters.
- Clarify integration test configuration comments to better describe env aliasing and information flow.

Documentation:
- Add testing architecture evaluation notes describing pre- and post-overhaul test quality and grading.
- Add evidence JSON documents with purpose/why/infoFlow metadata for testing and linting artefacts.

Tests:
- Add end-to-end chaos tests that verify graceful UI failure handling and recovery after transient API errors.
- Add unit tests for HTTP resilience utilities, including caller signal propagation, Retry-After parsing, and global fetch cleanup between tests.
- Add an integration env mock to support adapter testing without a live SvelteKit server.

Hey - I've found 1 issue, and left some high level feedback:

- The `isAbortError` helper currently relies on `error instanceof Error`, which may miss DOMExceptions in some environments; consider loosening this to a structural check on `name === 'AbortError'` (and possibly `code`) to improve cross-runtime robustness.
- `fetchWithTimeout` accepts any `timeoutMs` value and will abort immediately for `0` or negative values; it may be clearer either to validate `timeoutMs > 0` and throw on invalid input or explicitly document and test the current behavior as intentional.
- In `gotoHydrated` within `chaos.spec.ts`, the fixed `waitForTimeout(250)` is still a source of potential flakiness; consider replacing it with a deterministic wait on a hydration marker or specific UI element becoming ready instead of a hardcoded delay.

<details>
<summary>Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

~~~markdown
Please address the comments from this code review:

## Overall Comments
- The `isAbortError` helper currently relies on `error instanceof Error`, which may miss DOMExceptions in some environments; consider loosening this to a structural check on `name === 'AbortError'` (and possibly `code`) to improve cross-runtime robustness.
- `fetchWithTimeout` accepts any `timeoutMs` value and will abort immediately for `0` or negative values; it may be clearer either to validate `timeoutMs > 0` and throw on invalid input or explicitly document and test the current behavior as intentional.
- In `gotoHydrated` within `chaos.spec.ts`, the fixed `waitForTimeout(250)` is still a source of potential flakiness; consider replacing it with a deterministic wait on a hydration marker or specific UI element becoming ready instead of a hardcoded delay.

## Individual Comments

### Comment 1
<location path="src/lib/core/http-resilience.ts" line_range="78-87" />
<code_context>
+	for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**issue:** The post-loop AbortError throw is effectively unreachable and the explanatory comment is misleading.

With this control flow the loop always either returns a `Response` or throws from inside the loop; execution never reaches the final `throw lastAbortError ?? ...`. On the last attempt, `AbortError` is re-thrown immediately because `attempt < maxAttempts` is false, so `lastAbortError` and the trailing `throw` are effectively dead code. Please either remove them or restructure the loop if you want a single exit that uses the accumulated abort error.
</issue_to_address>
~~~

</details>
